command: claude CLI 2.1.285 print mode (claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --no-session-persistence --system-prompt <porting system prompt>, prompt file on stdin, run from an empty directory)
notes:
Defects of the original kept (behaviour unchanged, each commented in the code):
- On LENGERR, LOG-LEN logs the START record's full original length (what CICS puts in LENGTH), not the
  20 bytes actually moved into WS-DATA. A length of 10000 or more would also lose its high-order digit(s)
  in PIC 9(4). Fix: MOVE FUNCTION MIN(WS-LEN 20) TO LOG-LEN.
- Any RETRIEVE response other than NORMAL or LENGERR ends the loop quietly, as if it were end of data.
  That includes INVREQ, IOERR and NOTFND, not only ENDDATA. Fix: set WS-MORE to 'N' only on
  DFHRESP(ENDDATA) and abend on anything else.
- LOG-RESP is PIC 99 unsigned, so it keeps only the absolute value mod 100 of EIBRESP. That is harmless
  for the values RETRIEVE returns.

Facts:
- No fact is contradicted by the source. The uow_handlers RESP_CHECK (LENGERR, NORMAL at line 28) matches
  lines 32-33.

Assumptions:
- runTask records WRITEQ TS through task.writeqTs, because the harness compares task events. The
  generated writeqTsGtlogL41 (Spring TempStorage) is used only by executeGtwork.
- executeGtwork has no START data, so it runs the loop once against ENDDATA. It writes the single record
  "R=29 L=0000 D=" followed by 20 spaces.
- The WS-LOG bytes are encoded in EBCDIC IBM037. The CSD and the facts do not name the region's code
  page; if the region uses another EBCDIC page, change the EBCDIC constant.
- The unsigned PIC 99 / 9(4) DISPLAY digits are written as plain zoned digits (F0-F9) through that
  charset, without CobolRecords. These fields have no sign to overpunch.
- The DFHRESP values used: NORMAL=0, NOTFND=13, INVREQ=16, IOERR=17, LENGERR=22, ENDDATA=29.
